tip: With the third trimester beginning and baby's lungs and brain rapidly maturing, make it a habit to notice your baby's movement pattern daily and learn what 'normal for your baby' feels like, because by 28 weeks more than 90% of babies could survive with advanced care if born early, and changes in movement are one of the first signs midwives and doctors want you to call about—not something to ignore.
affirmation: I know my baby's normal patterns, and I trust myself to speak up if something doesn't feel right.
desc: Your baby is starting to put on weight more quickly now. You may also notice stronger kicks and stretches, partly because your baby is bigger and partly because movement patterns are getting more organized.
